notes: V-CTR-006 is "ActionRecord lifecycle: every legal transition succeeds, every illegal one is rejected (06 §4.3)". It was scheduled as test-writing over an existing rule and there was no rule. TWO DEFECTS IN SHIPPED CODE, both found by trying to write the check. (1) Nothing enforced the lifecycle anywhere: journal.Store.SetPhase accepted `Verified -> Pending`, `Rejected -> Executing` and `"" -> Undone`. The lifecycle existed only as an ASCII diagram in a doc comment, so 06 §4.3's status-RBAC rows -- ChatOps may write `PendingApproval -> Pending/Rejected` and nothing else, the undo controller `-> Undone` only -- were unenforceable in the one direction admission cannot cover: not who may write the field, but what the field may become. (2) `status.phase` was never populated at creation: `status` is a subresource, so client.Create sent the block and the API server dropped it, and only `Labels[kube-agents/status]` landed. Every record read back an empty phase while its label named one -- the exact inversion of 06 §4.3, which makes the field authoritative and the label derived -- so a parked record had no `PendingApproval` for the gateway's one permitted transition to leave from. WHAT IS NOW ASSERTED: the lifecycle is data in `api/v1alpha1/actionrecord_phases.go` and the check is a CLOSED TRUTH TABLE over all 121 ordered pairs (ten phases plus the empty from-phase), with the expected answer transcribed from 06 §4.3 a second time rather than read out of the production map -- a test that iterates the map to decide what to expect asserts the map equals itself and survives deleting every entry. Vacuity guards pin 27 legal cells and 94 refused. Both spellings (CanTransitionTo, ValidateActionPhaseTransition) must agree on every cell. The CRD kubebuilder enum is read out of actionrecord_types.go as data and cross-joined in both directions; reachability from the creation set is a real BFS; Successors() must hand back a copy; the four refusal diagnoses must stay distinct and name both ends. At the enforcement points: Create refuses a forged initial phase and writes nothing, Create persists the phase through the subresource, SetPhase validates against the RE-READ phase and not the caller's stale copy, and a retried Create does not rewind a record that has since advanced. A SPEC RULING, NOT A HALT: 06 §4.3's diagram draws `Failed -> RolledBack` while the same section's table marks Failed terminal. Settled from the spec's own principal list rather than from its picture -- no principal in the status-RBAC table can write that edge -- so the edge is dropped and the Terminal column is what the code implements. `Verified -> Undone` survives the same test for the opposite reason: terminal is a claim about the broker's pipeline, and Undone is a different principal, later. THE ESCAPE: the first sweep ran 11/12. M10, restoring defect (2) exactly, survived, because controller-runtime's fake client does not model the status subresource on Create -- `withStatusSubresource` is consulted in tracker.update and not in fakeClient.Create -- so the fake keeps a status block every real API server discards. That is the mechanism by which the defect survived five phases under a green suite: the assertion was green because the fake never dropped the field. Fixed at the helper, not in the one test that noticed: newFakeStore now installs a Create interceptor that zeroes Status before delegating, so the whole package is measured against the cluster it will run on. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this is the L1 half. Nothing here proves a real API server's admission stack refuses an illegal phase write from a principal other than the broker -- 06 §4.3's status-RBAC table is enforced by RBAC at L2 and that row is P9-T9b-5's. The ASCII diagram in the spec and in actionrecord_types.go is still uncorrected and is filed as a spec-art finding.
